approachQuestion.prompt:
Longest consecutive values

Return the length of the longest run of consecutive integer values present in an unsorted array; duplicates do not extend a run. Values are opaque comparison keys: hashing, radix, counting and bucket methods are excluded. 0≤n≤200000; values in ±10^9. Examples: [100,4,200,1,3,2,2]→4; []→0.

Do not modify either input. Values are opaque comparison keys; hashing, radix, counting and bucket methods are outside the stated model. Choose the most efficient valid method that returns the required result for every allowed input.
constraints: Inputs are read-only and must remain unchanged.
Only comparison-based ordering is allowed; hashing, radix, counting and bucket methods are outside this problem model.

options.text: Sort values, skip duplicates, and extend a run when the next distinct value is exactly previous+1.
options.feedback: Ordering makes each possible consecutive run adjacent; duplicate skipping prevents false breaks.
Gaps may be missing: [1,3] returns 3 though the longest run is 1.

options.text: Count adjacent consecutive pairs in the original array.
options.feedback: The array’s order is unrelated to numeric consecutiveness.

options.text: For every value, scan the full input repeatedly to test successive integers until one is absent.
options.feedback: Correct but repeated full scans can be avoided by sorting once.

feedback.reason: Equal neighbors do not extend a consecutive run and must not reset it either.
details: Sort the values, skip duplicates, and maintain the current run length while scanning adjacent distinct values.
Equal neighbors do not extend a consecutive run and must not reset it either. Only a distinct value exactly one larger extends the current run; a larger gap begins a new run.
“Sort values, skip duplicates, and extend a run when the next distinct value is exactly previous+1.”: Ordering makes each possible consecutive run adjacent; duplicate skipping prevents false breaks.
“Return max(values)−min(values)+1.”: Gaps may be missing: [1,3] returns 3 though the longest run is 1.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method revealed below, choose the tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space bounds. Count working copies, event/heap/visited storage and sort buffers; exclude the caller input and returned output. Comparisons and arithmetic take constant time; merge sort uses a linear buffer.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space
O(n log n) time, O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Sort values, then scan adjacent distinct values once.
details: Comparison merge sort processes the copied values in O(n) work per merge level and O(log n) levels. The distinct-neighbor run scan adds only O(n). Copy and merge buffer are O(n) auxiliary space. Skipping duplicates does not skip the sort, and no nested pair enumeration justifies quadratic time.
